item.text: The Corruption and Crime Commission monitored and reviewed a police investigation into an arrest and custody incident in a country town.
item.support: The Commission closely monitored its progress and reviewed the final report.

item.text: Its review considered a police vehicle's use, force in custody, supervision, medical care and missing custody records.
item.support: Failure to record Mr Rhodes' custody status at any stage was a serious omission.

item.text: The Commission considered police handling of the use-of-force matter appropriate and found the decision to use managerial action rather than prosecution was available on the facts.
item.support: In the Commission's opinion, the decision to proceed with managerial rather than prosecution action was fairly open to be made on the facts.

item.text: Its four recommendations covered tailored training for repeated excessive force, custody management, custody officer experience and reporting injury or severe discomfort.
item.support: Consideration should be given to ensuring that custody officers have sufficient training and experience to carry out their duties.

item.quote: The outcome of the investigation and the action taken by the WA Police Force against the officers appears reasonable and appropriate.
